_comment: Anonymized example config showing every strategy and every target. Drop into ~/.config/keyrotate/<your-project-name>.json and adjust.

GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY._note: DON'T cron-rotate this — it encrypts user OAuth refresh tokens; rotation invalidates them all.

manualSteps: Revoke the old key in the same dashboard after a successful LLM request.

MAILJET_API_KEY._note: Rotate together with MAILJET_SECRET_KEY (both halves of the same pair).
manualSteps: Open https://app.mailjet.com/account/apikeys → 'Add a new API key' (don't regenerate the old one — zero-downtime cutover).
After verifying email send, delete the old key pair in Mailjet.

TEST_USER_PASSWORD._note: Composite target — bcrypts the new password into MongoDB users.{username}.password AND pushes the plaintext to GitHub Actions secrets so test runners can log in.

NAS_DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAT._note: Read-only PAT a NAS cron uses to `git pull`. After `secret set`, the value lands at the configured ssh.path on the remote (chmod 600). GitHub PATs can't be created via API, so manual strategy; manualSteps below documents the UI flow.
manualSteps: Repository access: only the repo(s) the NAS clones. Permissions: Contents Read-only + Metadata Read-only. Expiry: 1 year.
secret set example NAS_DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAT --value <NEW_TOKEN>   # ssh writes it to /var/secrets/github_pat
Test: SSH in and run the cron job's git-pull step manually.

PROVISIONING_DOC_URL._note: Inventory-only entry: tracked here so `secret list example` shows it and `secret notes example PROVISIONING_DOC_URL` surfaces the playbook, but propagation is fully manual (no targets). Use this pattern for secrets that live somewhere keyrotate can't reach (a vendor portal, a one-off SaaS without an API, etc.).
manualSteps: Generate / rotate the credential by hand.
Update wherever it's consumed (no automated propagation).

ALLOWED_ORIGINS._note: Not a secret — comma-separated CORS allowlist. Tracked so updates propagate everywhere with `secret add` / `secret remove`.
